newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI SHARES SEEN MATCHING MARKET.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI SHARES SEEN MATCHING MARKET.

text.p: Analysts see the current rise in shares of the largest Czech commercial bank, Komercni banka a.s., as a reflection of overall positive market sentiment in recent weeks, and not based on the bank's fundamentals.

"We cannot find the circumstances permitting the increase in share price of Komercni Banka a.s. from the financial results, but from the whole situation ruling the Czech capital markets," said Tomas Cikrt, analyst at Akro Capital in Prague.

Komercni has risen by 11.5 percent in the last four weeks, closing unchanged at 2,650 on Monday, and slightly outpreforming the market which has shown an overall increase in top stocks of roughly 11 percent in the period.
Zivnostenska Banka anaylsts Pavel Sobisek said he believed Komercni would follow the market until it publishes its 1996 resultsin March.
Only an unexpected result could move the price, he said.
"If the net profit ranges between 4.9 and 5.2 billion crowns, the market will evaluate it neutrally," said Sobisek.
Komercni posted 5.2 billion crowns net profit in 1995, up from 1.7 billion crowns in the previous year, according to Czech accounting standards.
While most analysts said that investors are buying up blue-chip Czech stocks as part of a spree on the market as a whole, Komercni was still a good long-term investment.
"After colourless autumn, there have been almost solely positive impulses coming to the market since the beginning of the year," said Cikrt.
He noted the preparation of a new market watchdog and other increased activity of the market supervison, plus better than expected company results, as news which pushed the market higher.
Cikrt said a recent wave of crown Eurobond issues also incrased the interest in Czech shares, and that foreign investors have been moving in from the overpriced Polish and Hungarian markets.

Komercni -- the largest local bank with a balance sheet totalling 432 billion crowns at the end of the third quarter, and equity capital of 9.5 billion -- ranks second in terms of deposits, and first in terms of loans granted.
Rudolf Kaninsky of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., said Komercni managed to largely reduce its proportion of doubtful loans, and has improved its capital adequacy.

"Further growth of (Komercni's share) price will be suported mainly by a demand of foreign investors, for whom Komercni shares are liquid enough and promise certain dividend and capital gain for acceptable risk," said Kaninsky.
Cikrt, however said he expected a short-term decline of Komercni shares.
"At the price around 2,650 we recommend to speculate on a temporary decline," he said.
